title: Capacity Playbook Cadence and Initiative Symphony — Q3 Roadmap
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: produce a tightly scoped Q3 roadmap that treats Dedicated Capacity and Autoscale as a single product surface — clear milestones, an experimentation matrix, financial guardrails, and an operational runbook.

Scope: dedicated pool sizing UX, autoscale policy primitives (headroom / prewarm / surge), reservation lifecycle (hedging + fractional shares), cost observability hooks, and canary + fallback rollout plans.

Outcomes we will deliver by end of quarter:
- A prioritized initiative list with measurable success metrics and owner assignment.
- Experimentation matrix (3x3) mapping customer segments x surge patterns to autoscale tactics.
- Financial model showing per-token unit cost delta across strategies (prewarm vs on-demand vs fractional reservation).
- Playbook for canarying autoscale + dedicated failover with SLOs and rollback triggers.

Why this is different: instead of only adding more autoscale knobs, this initiative centers on the cadence and decision-making around capacity commitments — when to reserve, when to hedge, and how to automate fallbacks with predictable economics for customers.

comments: 2026-01-12: Kickoff with Eng + Infra + Platform PMs. Agreed to focus first on 2 customer archetypes: AI-native PLG and Enterprise SLO-focused workloads.
2026-01-18: Eng spike completed. Kernel-level prewarm hook adds ~6% baseline cost but reduces tail latency by ~45ms for 99th percentile. Notes in ENG-20914 spike doc.
2026-01-25: Finance flagged unit-cost assumptions — need to validate pricing sensitivity for fractional reservations. Action: run Monte Carlo sim (ENG-21500).
2026-01-30: Design prototyped reservation UI with hedging slider. Initial feedback from CE team: must expose SLAs and rollback visibility for enterprises.
2026-02-02: PM review: consolidate experiment matrix, assign owners for canary run (Asha/Puneet/Diego). Next sync with Sales on 2026-02-07 to align adoption pilots.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritized backlog with clear milestones and owners for each initiative (published to the roadmap by 2026-02-15)
Experimentation matrix with at least 6 planned experiments and measurement plan (latency, cost, success-rate)
Financial model validated with >=3 historical customer traces and sensitivity slices
Operational runbook drafted with SLOs, canary criteria, rollback triggers, and postmortem template
Design prototypes for reservation hedging and autoscale policy UX reviewed and approved by Design lead
risks: Engineering capacity: kernel + scheduling work collides with runtime-2.4 stabilization window (mitigation: reserve a 2-sprint buffer)
Customer churn risk if early adopters see cost spikes during experiments (mitigation: opt-in pilots + credits)
Telemetry gaps: missing per-route token-level cost attribution could block financial validation (ENG-21500 dependency)
Complexity: too many knobs exposed to customers will slow adoption (mitigation: default profiles and recommended templates)
Cross-team alignment: Sales/Support need clear messaging on reservation hedging semantics to avoid confusion
